data.title: Protection on Hayame
data.summary: How Hayame keeps renters, hosts and cars safe: who we verify, how money and deposits are handled, what to do if something goes wrong, and what Hayame does and does not cover.

highlights.title: Everyone is checked
highlights.body: Renters send a face photo and both sides of their driving licence before they can pay. Hosts are verified with a government ID before they can list.

highlights.title: Money goes through Hayame
highlights.body: You pay securely with Paystack. If the host declines, you are refunded in full.

highlights.title: Deposits are protected by evidence
highlights.body: A deposit can only be reduced for a real cost backed by photos, receipts or a report.

highlights.title: Hayame is not an insurer
highlights.body: The car is covered by the host's own motor insurance. Hayame does not sell insurance today.

questions.q: What does protection mean on Hayame?
a: Protection is the set of checks and rules that make a trip safe for both sides. It covers who is allowed to book and list, how payments and deposits are held, the record we keep of every trip, and the help you get from our team when there is a problem.
It is not an insurance policy. Read "Is the car insured?" below so you know exactly where you stand before you drive.

questions.q: Is Hayame a car rental company?
a: No. Hayame is a marketplace. Cars belong to their hosts, and the rental agreement for each trip is between the renter and the host. Hayame provides the app, takes the payment, keeps the trip record and steps in to help when the two sides cannot agree.

questions.q: Is the car insured?
a: Every host must keep valid motor insurance on the car and confirm with their insurer that it may be hired out. That policy, with its own limits and exclusions, is the cover on the trip.

Hayame does not provide or sell bundled insurance at the moment. If a listing shows an insurance amount at checkout, that is set by the host and described on the listing. If you need more cover, ask the host in the chat before you book, or speak to your own insurer.

Whatever cover exists may not apply if the rules are broken, for example if someone other than the verified renter drives, or the car is used as a taxi or driven after drinking. In that case the renter carries the full cost.

questions.q: Why do I have to send a photo of my face and my driving licence?
a: Hosts are handing over a valuable car. Before your first booking we check that you are a real person, that you hold a valid licence, and that the person collecting the car is the person who booked it.

You send three photos: your face, and the front and back of your licence. Our team reviews them, usually within a few hours, and emails you as soon as you are approved. You only do this once, unless your licence expires or we need to check again.

questions.q: Who can see my licence and face photo?
a: Only the Hayame team members who review verifications. They are stored privately and are never shown to hosts or other users.

questions.q: How are hosts checked?
a: Anyone who wants to list a car applies with a government-issued ID and their details, and is approved by our team before their first listing. Every car listing is also reviewed before it appears. Verified hosts are marked on their profile and listings.

questions.q: Can I book a car for someone else to drive?
a: No. The person who books is the person who drives. You may not rent on behalf of another person or hand the car to anyone else. A second driver is only allowed if the host agrees to that named person in the Hayame chat before they drive, and that person has their own verified Hayame account.
Hosts are asked to check that the person collecting the car matches the booking and their licence, and to refuse the handover if they do not.

questions.q: Is it safe to pay through the app?
a: Yes. Payments are processed by Paystack, by mobile money, card or bank transfer. Your card details are entered on Paystack's secure page and are never stored by Hayame.

Always pay inside Hayame. If someone asks you to pay them directly, by cash or mobile money outside the app, decline and report it. A trip paid for outside Hayame has no deposit handling, no refund rights and no support from us.

questions.q: What happens to my money if the host says no?
a: Unless a listing offers instant booking, the host has to accept your request. If the host declines or does not respond, you are refunded in full, including the deposit.

questions.q: What is the refundable deposit for?
a: Some listings include a security deposit. It is shown as its own line before you pay. It is there to cover real costs that come up from the trip, such as new damage, missing fuel, a late return, heavy cleaning, or a traffic fine or toll.
If nothing is owed, the whole deposit comes back to you after the trip. If you cancel before the trip, the deposit is always returned in full.

questions.q: Can a host keep my deposit for no reason?
a: No. A deduction has to be for a real cost and supported by evidence: handover and return photos, a receipt or repair quote, a fine notice or a police report. If you disagree, open a dispute in the app and our team will look at what both sides have provided before anything is decided.

questions.q: What should I do at pick-up and return?
a: Walk around the car with the host and take clear photos of every side, the inside, the fuel gauge and the mileage. Do the same at return. Photos taken at handover are the best protection either side has: if there is a disagreement later, they are the first thing our team asks for.

Check that you have the spare tyre and tools, that the lights and brakes work, and that the car matches the listing. If something is wrong, tell the host in the chat before you drive away so there is a record.

questions.q: What do I do if there is an accident?
a: Make sure everyone is safe first. In an emergency call 112, or the police on 191, the fire service on 192 or an ambulance on 193.

Then tell the host and Hayame straight away through the app. Report to the Ghana Police Service where anyone is hurt, another vehicle or property is involved, or the law requires it, and get a police report. Take photos of the scene, the vehicles and any other driver's details. Do not admit fault, do not leave the car, and do not arrange repairs yourself.

questions.q: What if the car breaks down?
a: Stop somewhere safe and message the host in the app. A fault that existed before the trip, or ordinary mechanical failure, is the host's responsibility, and the host should arrange help or a replacement. If the trip cannot continue through no fault of yours, contact us and we will help you with a fair refund for the unused days.
Damage caused by how the car was driven, for example driving through flood water or on a road the car is not suited to, is the renter's responsibility.

questions.q: What if the car is stolen?
a: Report it to the police immediately and tell the host and Hayame through the app. Keep the keys and give them to the host. Cars on Hayame may be fitted with a tracker, which the host and Hayame can use to help recover the car.

questions.q: Who pays for traffic fines, tolls and towing?
a: The renter pays any fine, toll, parking charge, towing or impound fee that arises during the trip, even if the notice arrives after the trip has ended.

questions.q: Who pays if the car is damaged?
a: From handover until return, the renter is responsible for the car. The renter pays for new damage and for reasonable recovery costs, except where the host's insurance pays, or where the damage was caused by the host or by a fault that was already there.
Normal wear, such as light stone chips or tyre wear from ordinary driving, is not damage.

questions.q: How is my car protected when I host?
a: Every renter is verified with a face photo and driving licence before they can pay. You see who is booking, you can accept or decline requests (unless you choose instant booking), and you can ask questions in the chat first.

You can set a security deposit on your listing, a surcharge for trips outside your region, and your own cancellation policy. Payment is collected before the trip, and the trip record, messages and photos are kept so that a claim can be reviewed fairly.

questions.q: What do I need to have in place before I list?
a: You must own the car or have the owner's written permission, and it must be registered, roadworthy and insured for hire. Keep your documents current, service the car, and describe it honestly. At handover, check the renter's face and licence against the booking and take photos together.

questions.q: A renter returned my car damaged or late. What do I do?
a: Take photos straight away, message the renter in the chat, and open a dispute in the app within 24 hours of the trip ending. Add your handover photos, the return photos and any quote or receipt. Our team will review both sides and decide how the deposit is applied. If the cost is more than the deposit, the renter still owes the balance.

questions.q: How do I report a problem?
a: Message the other person in the Hayame chat first; most issues are settled there. If that does not work, open a dispute from the booking, or contact support. Report trip problems within 24 hours of the trip ending so the evidence is fresh.

questions.q: How does Hayame decide a dispute?
a: We look at the booking, the messages, the handover and return photos, and any receipts, quotes or reports from both sides. We may ask either of you for more information. Decisions about deposits are based on that evidence, and we tell both sides the outcome.

questions.q: What is Hayame not responsible for?
a: Hayame does not own or inspect the cars and cannot guarantee the condition of a vehicle or the behaviour of any user. We are not an insurer and do not pay for damage, injury, theft or loss arising from a trip. Our responsibility is to run the platform properly, handle payments and deposits as described, and deal with reports fairly. The full detail is in our Terms of Service.

data.contact: Need help now? Use Help in the app or email support@hayamegh.com. In an emergency call 112 first.
